grants.programme: Membership — defamation and legal-threat defence cover
grants.summary: A membership organisation, created by investigative journalists (OCCRP) and lawyers at the Cyrus R. Vance Center, that pools member contributions into a mutual defence fund to cover legal costs of defending public-interest investigative reporting against defamation and other lawfare/SLAPP-style threats. Membership includes pre-publication risk review, response drafting when members receive legal threats, and litigation defence by a specialist media-lawyer network.

amount.note: Membership fee, not a cash grant; reported floor around $1,000 with an average around $3,500 depending on level of legal service, with subsidies available in some cases (figures per third-party press coverage, not directly confirmed on the funder's own page today).

grants.notes: This still checks out as the org's core (only) programme; no separate grant/fund found. Note the working domain is reporters-shield.org (with hyphen) - the source's recorded URL reportersshield.org (no hyphen) may be outdated or a redirect; worth checking. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A free, 24/7 rapid-response service providing real-time technical assistance and cybersecurity advice to civil society groups, activists, media organisations, journalists, bloggers, and human rights defenders facing digital threats. The Helpline aims to respond to all requests within two hours and offers support in ten languages.

amount.note: Provides technical assistance, not a cash grant.

grants.notes: Today's accessnow.org snapshot covered the general 'Access Now Grants' grassroots-grantmaking page and a donor financial log, neither of which detailed the Helpline; details confirmed via web search of the funder's /help/ page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: ARIJ — Arab Reporters for Investigative Journalism
grants.summary: ARIJ awards grants of US$2,500 to Arab journalists to produce digital, audio, or televised investigative reports exposing environmental, legal, and financial corruption, separately covering filming and editing expenses. ARIJ's own site nav invites ongoing submission of investigation proposals ('قدم تحقيقاً') alongside editorial mentoring and fact-checking support.

amount.note: US$2,500 per investigative report grant; ARIJ separately covers filming/video-editing expenses.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot of arij.net again only captured the Arabic homepage, supporters and support-us pages (did not reach ARIJ's dedicated grants page); a corroborating web search of ARIJ's own site (en.arij.net) confirms the $2,500 grant amount, the eligible-country list, that joint/cross-border pitches are welcomed, and that female journalists are specifically encouraged to apply. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A year-long, non-residential fellowship for activists, investigative journalists, filmmakers and lawyers to collaboratively investigate one pressing social-justice issue chosen around an annual theme. Reported support has included a fellow stipend, project funding, and a 'connect fund' for collaboration, plus training, mentorship and networking.

amount.note: Previously reported (secondary sources, prior cycle): fellow stipend up to US$64,900, project funding up to US$10,000, and a connect fund up to US$5,000.

grants.notes: Re-fetched 2026-10-03: snapshot again confirms the programme exists ('Fellowships for Activists, Investigative Journalists, Filmmakers and Lawyers to spend a year working on one pressing social justice challenge') and states verbatim: BERTHA FOUNDATION DOES NOT ACCEPT UNSOLICITED PROPOSALS — applications are only taken during announced windows. No new 2026/2027 call was visible on today's snapshot; the most recent verified deadline (28 Jul 2025) remains the latest confirmed window. Amount figures remain from prior-cycle secondary reporting. Not confirmed on the funder's own page for deadline/amount specifics.

grants.summary: Craig Newmark Philanthropies accepts funding proposals from registered nonprofits on a rolling basis across its focus areas, one of which is 'Promoting the Truth'; a separate portal exists only for veterans/military-family support. Applicants must supply proof of active 501(c)(3)/public-charity status with the IRS and Secretary of State, and CNP says it cannot review or fund every request. Multi-year commitments are released annually based on progress and the effectiveness of the grantee's communication and collaboration.

amount.note: Application asks for a 'grant amount requested' but no published range.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot of craignewmarkphilanthropies.org/apply reconfirms this process verbatim: rolling review, 'Sometimes we'll invite informal proposals, but final proposals ... must be submitted below', IRS/Secretary-of-State proof-of-status requirements, and 'We apologize in advance that we can't review and fund every request.' Separate prior reporting (Nieman Lab, Jan 2026) quoted Craig Newmark describing a pullback from journalism funding toward cybersecurity/safety-of-journalists priorities, so real-world receptiveness to new 'Promoting the Truth' proposals may be narrower than the page implies — that caveat is from secondary reporting, not the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Balkan Trust for Democracy (German Marshall Fund)
grants.programme: BTD Support for Western Balkans 6 — Media Freedom track
grants.summary: The Balkan Trust for Democracy funds civil society organisations registered in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia. One of its two current thematic tracks is strengthening media freedom (the other combats domestic and gender-based violence), delivered as a sub-granting scheme realised with Norway's development cooperation (an added NOK 20 million) and the Royal Norwegian Embassy in Belgrade.
grants.notes: Re-checked on 2026-10-04: today's snapshot of gmfus.org again only captured generic GMF organisational/press pages and never reached Balkan Trust for Democracy's own grant-call pages, so this entry remains built from a web search of GMF's own site, which confirms the programme's two priority areas (media freedom; domestic/gender-based violence), the six-country WB6 scope, and Norwegian government co-funding. Only registered civil-society organisations in the six WB6 countries may apply — not individual freelancers. No corroborated deadline was found; a separate EU/EEAS 'WB6 MEDIA' programme and a distinct Western Balkans Fund grassroots-grant call exist with their own deadlines and should not be conflated with this BTD call. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Healthy Information Sphere (International Human Rights Programme)
grants.summary: Oak Foundation's Healthy Information Sphere portfolio, within its International Human Rights Programme, supports independent journalism, media pluralism, digital rights and information integrity work aimed at holding power to account. Not-for-profit organisations not already invited by a programme officer may submit an unsolicited Letter of Enquiry through Oak's online form, though the Foundation states it has no open call for proposals and funds only a small share of the enquiries it receives.

amount.note: Not stated publicly; programme budgets are reported to be allocated roughly a year in advance and only a small number of unsolicited enquiries are funded each year.

grants.notes: Reconfirmed via WebSearch (no fresh snapshot available): the submit-enquiry online form remains Oak's only unsolicited intake mechanism; Oak responds within about two months if more information is needed or a formal proposal is invited. This is a general unsolicited-Letter-of-Enquiry intake, not a journalism-specific open call, and the Foundation has previously stated it has no open call for proposals at this time. Geographic focus reported as EU, US, UK, Brazil and other 'global East' geographies, so global scope is uncertain. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: MDIF provides loans, equity investments, loan guarantees and related business advisory support to independent media and information businesses operating in countries with a history of media oppression, ownership concentration, a state of democratic transition, or information poverty. This is investment capital rather than grant funding; applicants must be independent of government or other interest groups, complete an inquiry form, and go through a multi-step due-diligence process. A current sub-line, MDIF Ventures, invests in young/growing media companies with social impact and scaling potential, and a regional Western Balkans Fund window has also been reported.

amount.note: MDIF Ventures is reported to offer ongoing funding up to US$1,000,000 per investee; main MDIF financing is case-by-case with no published general range. MDIF's overall portfolio has been reported at roughly $118.7M across ~58-60 media businesses in 31-34 countries in prior reporting.

grants.notes: Reconfirmed via WebSearch: MDIF remains an investment fund (debt/equity), not a grantmaker — financing carries repayment or ownership terms. No snapshot of the funder's page was available this run. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: GNI Lab is a 12-week program combining virtual sessions, practical exercises and personalized mentoring that helps independent news creators and small digital media outlets strengthen their journalism using Google tools, audience-building practices, and revenue-diversification strategies. It is run by SembraMedia in partnership with the Google News Initiative for participants from Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru and Uruguay. The 2026 cohort's application window closed on August 2, 2026, and no confirmed date for a next cycle was found.

amount.note: Training and mentoring program; no cash grant amount was stated in search results.

grants.notes: Reconfirmed: the 2026 cohort's application window closed August 2, 2026. SembraMedia/Google News Initiative also run a related, possibly overlapping 'GNI Startups Lab Hispanoamérica' accelerator (up to 10 entrepreneurs + up to 10 media outlets, with financial support/training/consulting) — not recorded as a separate entry here because it is unclear whether it is the same recurring programme under a different name or a distinct one, and no confirmed current-cycle dates were found. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: PULSE, n-ost's cross-border journalism network ('Europe beyond the beat'), funds small reporting teams of two journalists from different eligible countries to produce collaborative stories under one of four Thematic Networks (media and society, media/AI legislation, digitalisation, and disinformation/fact-checking). The 2026 call was open to journalists with fiscal residency across a broad list of countries including EU and EU-candidate states, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Brazil, China, India, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Lebanon, Russia, the UK, the US, Uzbekistan, Belarus, Israel/Palestine and Iran, with two teams funded per network. The pitch deadline was extended to July 20, 2026, with results expected in September 2026, so this cycle is now closed to new applicants.

amount.note: Grant amount per team was not stated in search results.

grants.notes: The 2026 Thematic Network pitch deadline (extended to July 20, 2026) has passed. PULSE is reportedly changing format: coverage found today describes the project moving from rolling applications to fixed-deadline calls for 'Sprint Stories' and 'Deep Dive Series', with a first-call deadline around mid-July 2026 and a second call announced for 'Autumn 2026' -- but no exact second-call deadline or amount was stated in any source read, so no separate entry was created for it. The 2026 call's eligible journalist countries extend well beyond Europe (e.g. Brazil, China, India, US) even though the programme is Europe-focused; geoScope here reflects the programme's Europe focus, not the full eligibility list. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Media Forward Fund — General Funding Line
grants.summary: A recurring funding line (roughly three calls per year) offering up to EUR 400,000 per application to media organisations headquartered in the DACH region (Germany, Austria, Switzerland) developing new business models and revenue sources to sustain public-interest journalism.

amount.note: Up to €400,000 per application.

grants.notes: Today's erste-stiftung snapshot again did not surface this programme page (only the homepage and the unrelated Facing the Future Fellowship); details are from the Media Forward Fund's own site via web search, which indicates roughly three call windows per year (a recent one ran 9–20 February 2026) rather than a single annual deadline. The previously recorded '7 September 2026' opening date could not be re-confirmed this round, so opensAt is left null pending the next announced window. Eligibility requires the applicant organisation's registered headquarters to be in Germany, Austria or Switzerland. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Grants of EUR 25,000–35,000, covering up to 100% of costs (incl. 15% overheads) for up to 18 months, for projects involving organisations from at least 3 V4 countries (or 2 neighbouring V4 countries for cross-border projects). Supported areas include anti-corruption work with investigative journalists and watchdogs, and improving media/information literacy and resilience to disinformation.

amount.note: Covers up to 100% of costs including 15% overheads; project duration up to 18 months.

grants.notes: No snapshot exists for visegrad-fund; facts sourced via web search of the Fund's own site. Deadlines recur three times a year (1 Feb, 1 Jun, 1 Oct); the 1 October 2026 round has just closed (confirmed by the Fund's own announcement that the third 2026 call opened 1 September). Next expected call opens around 1 February 2027. Journalism/media projects are one of several eligible themes, not the fund's sole purpose. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: African Academy for Open Source Investigation (AAOSI) Fellowship
grants.summary: Stipend-based fellowships pairing journalists and civil-society researchers with veteran forensic analysts to learn open-source and social-media intelligence (OSINT/SOCMINT) investigation techniques over about four months. Rounds rotate through different African sub-regions (Sahel/West/East Africa in an early-2026 round; Southern Africa in a mid-2026 round), each with its own call and deadline.

amount.note: Described as stipend-based; specific amount not stated in available sources.

grants.notes: Today's code-for-africa snapshot was again only 19 words (JS-rendered, empty), so this is sourced entirely from web search. Confirms a recurring fellowship with multiple regional rounds per year: the Sahel/West Africa/East Africa round (Burkina Faso, Chad, Mali, Niger, Senegal, Benin, Cameroon, Guinea, Togo, Ethiopia, Somalia, South Sudan) had a deadline of 6 March 2026, and a separate Southern Africa round's deadline of 10 August 2026 has also now passed. Six fellowships per round, roughly four months. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Six stipend-based, six-month fellowships run by Code for Africa's African Fact-Checking Alliance (AFCA) for journalists and fact-checkers in Southern Africa, with editorial training and mentoring from CfA's PesaCheck, iLAB and AFCA teams to produce fact-checking work on regional mis/disinformation.

amount.note: Stipend-based; specific amount not stated in available sources.

grants.notes: Snapshot again too thin to use (19 words). 2026 round's eligibility was limited to Angola, Botswana, Comoros, DRC, Eswatini, Lesotho, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Seychelles, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe; deadline of 10 April 2026 has passed. Recurring annual programme, six-month fellowship term. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism
grants.programme: Report Women! Female Reporters Leadership Programme (FRLP) Fellowship
grants.summary: An annual fellowship for mid-career female investigative journalists in Nigeria, combining residential training on leadership and investigative reporting with six months of mentorship to produce investigative stories and leadership projects addressing gender gaps in newsrooms. Funded via the Report Women! project with Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation support.

amount.note: Financial stipend not stated; support described as residential training plus six months of mentorship.

grants.notes: No snapshot exists for wole-soyinka-centre. The sixth cohort's residential training ran 2–4 April 2025 (application deadline 18 February 2025); requires at least four years of post-NYSC experience and current or emerging leadership role. No 2026/2027 cohort call was found in this search round, so deadline is left null pending confirmation. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism
grants.programme: CMEDIA Story Support: Strengthening Local Accountability
grants.summary: Under the Collaborative Media Engagement for Development, Inclusivity, and Accountability (CMEDIA) project, WSCIJ invites investigative story pitches from Nigerian journalists on subnational (state and local) government issues such as health, education, infrastructure, public spending, environment and social justice. Selected journalists research, write and publish the resulting stories. Funded by the MacArthur Foundation.

amount.note: Amount not stated in available sources.

grants.notes: This round's exact window is now confirmed via web search: opened 16 April 2026 and closed 30 April 2026 (previously recorded as an unconfirmed estimate). Proposals must interrogate governance, service delivery, human rights, public spending, environment, health, education or social justice at the local/state level. Part of the recurring CMEDIA project; next round's dates not yet known. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Ten scholarships of up to USD 2,100 each, run with Open Society Foundations, to support an investigative journalism project reported through a solutions-journalism lens. Past editions have focused on specific Central American countries (El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua); the programme runs in successive regional editions.

amount.note: Up to USD 2,100 per fellow; 10 fellowships awarded per edition. Selected journalists get 45 days to research and publish, with Fundación Gabo mentorship.

grants.notes: No snapshot exists for fundacion-gabo (its convocatorias page is JS-rendered Spanish-language content). Searched in Spanish; runs as successive regional editions (e.g. 'Triángulo Norte y Nicaragua'); exact current-edition deadline could not be confirmed, so left null. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Fundación Gabo's flagship scholarship programme, now in its seventh edition, funds journalism projects by journalists, journalism teams and content creators reporting on a chosen theme in Mexico and/or Colombia. At least 10 scholarships of USD 2,500–4,000 are awarded, plus up to USD 10,000 for transnational collaborations, with mentorship from Fundación Gabo's own instructors.

amount.note: 7th edition (2026): at least 10 scholarships of USD 2,500–4,000 each, up to USD 10,000 for transnational collaborations.

grants.notes: Geographic focus and amounts updated: the 7th edition (deadline 21 September 2026, now closed) was limited to Mexico and/or Colombia with the amounts above, replacing the previously recorded broader Latin-America-wide, 25-scholarship/USD 2,500–8,000 figures from an earlier edition — this programme's country focus and amounts appear to change each edition, so figures should be re-checked each cycle. Searched in Spanish. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Grants co-run with partner foundations (e.g. Fundación Avina, Habitat for Humanity) supporting investigative journalism on sustainable-development themes in Latin America, such as inclusive recycling or habitat. Winners receive a cash stipend plus access to editorial mentorship; the amount and theme change with each themed edition.

amount.note: Varies by themed edition: 2024 edition paid USD 3,000 per collaborative project and USD 1,000 per individual project; an earlier 'Edición Hábitat' round cited an USD 800 stipend.

grants.notes: Runs as a series of themed editions with different co-funders and topics (recycling, habitat, etc.); no current (2026) edition or open call was found this round, only the 2024 edition's figures, so marked closed pending a new announced cycle. Searched in Spanish. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Judith Neilson Institute for Journalism and Ideas
grants.summary: JNI's general grants programme funds journalists and media organisations to produce public-interest journalism, with a particular focus on Australian reporting and on Asia. Freelancers are advised to apply with the backing of a media platform.

amount.note: Amount not stated.

grants.notes: Re-searched 2026-10-04 (no working snapshot of jninstitute.org could be fetched this round either). News coverage continues to indicate JNI adopted a revised strategy under which it will no longer award grants to major news organisations, following organisational turbulence and a leadership transition; the institute was reported to still hold roughly $72m of its original $100m endowment. Scope and current application status of smaller/individual grants could not be confirmed directly on the funder's site. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Judith Neilson Institute for Journalism and Ideas (with the Walkley Foundation)
grants.summary: A grant administered with the Walkley Foundation to help Australian and permanent-resident freelance journalists produce a significant body of work, in any medium, reporting on Asia.

amount.note: Up to $25,000 cited in prior reporting; currency not explicitly stated (the programme is Australian-run).

grants.notes: Restricted to Australian citizens/permanent residents. This round of research could not reach walkleys.com directly to confirm whether a 2026/2027 round is active; no new evidence found either way. Kept as closed pending confirmation, consistent with JNI's 2026 strategy shift away from some legacy grant lines (see JNI Grants entry). Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A prototyping micro-grant fund helping news and media entrepreneurs in Asia ideate, launch, test and iterate news products and services. Splice does not take an equity stake in the ventures it supports.

amount.note: Described as micro-grants / pre-seed, non-equity funding; specific amount not stated.

grants.notes: For media startups/entrepreneurs building new news products, rather than individual freelance journalists. Search results now mostly surface 'Splice Beta' as an annual conference/event (e.g. 'Splice Beta 2026: Fork It', Chiang Mai, 7-9 Nov 2026) rather than fresh micro-grant cohorts; it is unclear from available search results whether the Beta Fund still runs an active grant-making cycle alongside the event or has been folded into it. Kept open pending direct confirmation. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: The sixth yearly Creative Europe cross-sectoral call funding transnational consortia of news media organisations on cross-border collaboration, sustainable business models and journalistic projects, including strand topics for economic resilience ('Collaborations') and support for media of particular democratic relevance such as local, community and investigative outlets ('Pluralism').

amount.note: 2026 round budget reported as €6.9m (an earlier report cited €13.8m); maximum grant per project €2,000,000; co-financing rate up to 80% of eligible costs.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot of culture.ec.europa.eu was only the generic Creative Europe landing/culture pages and did not mention this journalism-specific call, so this entry still relies on websearch. Requires a consortium of at least 3 independent entities from 3 different eligible countries (EU member states, EEA/associated countries, plus candidate countries such as Georgia and Ukraine); projects run ~24 months. The 2026 round's deadline (4 Feb 2026) has passed; as of 4 Oct 2026 no 2027 call fiche (CREA-CROSS-2027-JOURPART) could be found yet — it had not been published in prior years until around October of the preceding year, so a 2027 announcement may be imminent. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A Creative Europe cross-sectoral call funding innovative, cross-border media-literacy projects, open to consortia including media organisations, educational institutions and other bodies working to build public resilience against disinformation.

amount.note: Total indicative budget €3,000,000 for 2026; maximum grant per project €500,000; co-financing rate up to 70% of eligible costs.

grants.notes: Today's culture.ec.europa.eu snapshot did not cover this specific call (generic landing pages only). Requires a consortium of at least 3 entities from 3 different Creative Europe-participating countries; projects run up to 2 years. This round's deadline (11 March 2026) has passed; no 2027 edition found published yet as of 4 Oct 2026. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Nieman Foundation for Journalism, Harvard University
grants.summary: A fully funded academic-year fellowship for non-U.S. working journalists (including those working in the U.S.) to study at Harvard University, audit classes, and take part in Nieman seminars and events. Fellows receive a living stipend plus child care and health insurance allowances and must refrain from professional work during the fellowship year.

amount.note: $87,500 stipend paid over a nine-month period to cover living costs; additional child care allowance (up to $16,750/year for 4+ children) and health insurance supplement (up to $6,250) also available, per the funder's Stipend & Allowances page.

grants.notes: Re-confirmed via websearch (no snapshot attempted for nieman.harvard.edu this round): a recurring annual deadline of December 1 applies to the International Nieman Fellowship (e.g. Dec 1 2025 for the 2026-27 class). Nine-month academic-year fellowship, fellow relocates to Cambridge, MA. Requires 5+ years of full-time media experience (freelancers explicitly eligible); no PR/corporate-comms work; must speak/read/write English fluently; must not have done a residential fellowship of 4+ months in the prior 5 years. Must reside in Cambridge, MA during the fellowship and refrain from paid professional work except as approved. A designated Nieman-Berkman Klein Fellowship in Journalism Innovation track exists within the same application. Visa note (from prior verification): applicants from countries where the U.S. has suspended nonimmigrant (J) visas are advised to wait unless they hold another eligible citizenship.

grants.funder: Nieman Foundation for Journalism, Harvard University
grants.summary: A fully funded academic-year fellowship for U.S.-citizen working journalists (including those working outside the U.S.) to study at Harvard University, audit classes, and take part in Nieman seminars and events. Fellows receive a living stipend plus child care and health insurance allowances and must refrain from professional work during the fellowship year.

amount.note: $87,500 stipend paid over a nine-month period to cover living costs; additional child care allowance (up to $16,750/year for 4+ children) and health insurance supplement (up to $6,250) also available, per the funder's Stipend & Allowances page.

grants.notes: Re-confirmed via websearch: a recurring annual deadline of January 31 applies to the U.S. Nieman Fellowship. Nine-month academic-year fellowship, fellow relocates to Cambridge, MA. Same eligibility rules as the international track: 5+ years full-time media experience, freelancers explicitly eligible, no PR/corporate-comms work, English fluency required.

grants.funder: John S. Knight Journalism Fellowships, Stanford University
grants.summary: A nine-month residential fellowship at Stanford University for up to 20 journalists per year from around the world to work collaboratively on journalism's most urgent challenges, with personalized mentorship and access to Stanford classes. Recent cohorts received a stipend of $130,000, full Stanford tuition, health insurance, and support for spouses/partners/dependents.

amount.note: $130,000 stipend, full Stanford tuition and health insurance, plus support for spouses/partners/dependents, as reported for the 2026-27 cohort; figure not guaranteed to repeat for future cycles.

grants.notes: For the 2026-27 class (currently underway), applications opened 15 Oct 2025 and closed 3 Dec 2025 (Pacific time) per secondary reporting — no official page could be reached this round to confirm the dates for the 2027-28 cycle, which would be expected to open around mid-October 2026 based on this pattern but had not been confirmed as of 4 Oct 2026. Nine-month residential fellowship in Stanford, California; fellow relocates for the term. Up to 20 fellows/year, drawn from newsrooms, freelancers, and organisations supporting journalists; minimum 5 years' experience required, no degree required. Fellows have a personal coach (director) throughout the year; partners ('affiliates') are welcome at most gatherings. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, University of Oxford
grants.summary: A programme for practising, mid-career journalists and editors to spend three or six months in Oxford researching a personal project, with most fellows fully funded (fees, monthly stipend, travel and visa costs covered). Fellowships begin in October, January or April and require a minimum of five years' journalistic experience; freelancers may apply but those in PR/corporate communications may not.

amount.note: Most fellows are fully funded: fees covered plus a monthly stipend of £2,000 to cover accommodation, food and general living expenses, with travel to/from the UK and visa costs also covered. Some fellows instead come via sponsoring organisations with their own funding and selection process (e.g. Thomson Reuters Foundation Fellowship, Mona Megalli Fellowship for a Middle East journalist).

grants.notes: Re-searched 4 Oct 2026 (no snapshot of reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk attempted this round). Secondary sources conflict: several SEO/aggregator reposts still show a stale 'applications open, deadline 13 Feb' notice for the 2026-27 cohort, but a more recent aggregator explicitly states applications for the 2026-27 academic year are closed and will reopen in January 2027. Kept as 'upcoming' consistent with the latter, more current read. Fellowship lasts three or six months in Oxford, UK; fellow relocates for the term. Requires 5+ years' journalistic experience; open to journalists worldwide; not open to PR/public affairs/corporate communications staff; fellows must plan to return to journalism afterward. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Wallace House Center for Journalists, University of Michigan
grants.summary: An eight-month residential fellowship (late August through April) at the University of Michigan for journalists with at least five years of experience, including freelancers, to pursue a self-directed course of study. The programme includes a living stipend, relocation allowance, health insurance, and University of Michigan course auditing, with typically up to six international fellows joining ten to twelve U.S. journalists each year.

amount.note: Reported as an $85,000 stipend disbursed monthly August through April, plus a $5,000 relocation allowance and health insurance coverage. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.notes: No snapshot available for this source; sourced via WebSearch of secondary pages referencing wallacehouse.umich.edu content, not the funder's own page directly. Eight-month residential fellowship, Ann Arbor, Michigan; fellow relocates for the term. International applications for the 2026-27 cohort are described as closed, with applications for 2027-28 said to open in October 2026 (exact date not given). Up to six international fellows typically join ten to twelve U.S. journalists; international finalists are interviewed in January/February to allow time for visa processing. Requires 5+ years of journalism experience. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A three-month fellowship at the IWM in Vienna giving European journalists time off from their regular duties to pursue in-depth, independent research on a topic of their choice. Fellows receive a monthly stipend plus office space and access to the IWM academic community.

amount.note: Monthly stipend for the 3-month term.

grants.notes: Term runs three consecutive months, placement at the IWM in Vienna, between September 2026 and June 2027 for the cohort tied to this deadline. Open to European journalists (including Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Turkey) with several years' professional experience in print, broadcast or online journalism; no explicit language requirement stated. The 16 January 2026 deadline for this cycle has passed; the call recurs annually but the next deadline is not yet confirmed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Grants and Investments — Storytelling grants (Explorer Level I/II)
grants.summary: National Geographic Society's Explorer grants fund project leaders in conservation, education, research, storytelling and technology; the storytelling category explicitly covers journalism, photography, filmmaking and digital media. The Society has moved to a request-for-proposals model with themed windows rather than a standing rolling call.

amount.note: Level I grants up to $20,000; Level II grants up to $100,000 for established applicants pushing for significant impact.

grants.notes: Applicants must be 18+; those working outside their home country must include a local collaborator. The Society's own page currently lists no open opportunities and states a storytelling-related application window opens 1 October 2026; specific deadline and amount for that window were not stated in available evidence. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: National Geographic Society (with The Climate Pledge)
grants.programme: National Geographic Society × The Climate Pledge Storytelling Grant
grants.summary: A partnership between the National Geographic Society and The Climate Pledge funding storytelling projects on climate resilience, energy transition and sustainability solutions. Open to professional storytellers, journalists, documentary filmmakers, photographers, writers and podcast producers worldwide, whether or not they have previously held National Geographic Explorer status.

amount.note: Up to $100,000; early-career applicants (5 years or less experience) advised to request no more than $20,000. Project implementation period up to 2 years.

grants.funder: Heinrich Böll Stiftung (Washington, DC / North America Office)
grants.summary: Supports journalists based in the US, Canada or Germany (and, for Global South-focused stories, journalists in Africa, Asia and Latin America) to research and report transatlantic stories on climate & energy, democracy, foreign & security, technology, or global development policy. Fellows choose either an on-the-ground track including travel or a remote/digital track.

amount.note: Reported as $2,000 for the digital/remote track (no travel) and $4,000 for the on-the-ground track (with travel); figures not verified on the funder's own page.

grants.notes: Run out of the Heinrich Böll Stiftung's Washington, DC office rather than the German headquarters site. Exact current-cycle deadline and amount could not be confirmed on the funder's own page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung — Media Programme South East Europe
grants.summary: A scholarship for Bachelor's students (from their 2nd academic year) and Master's students of any major who are already actively engaged at a media outlet, at universities across South-East Europe. Scholars receive a monthly grant and access to exchanges with regional and international media experts.

amount.note: Monthly grant amount not stated in the pages reviewed.

grants.notes: Applicants must show a distinctive interest in social/political issues and alignment with KAS's values (democracy, freedom, rule of law, pluralism, European unification). Universities in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Romania and Serbia are covered. Most recently reported call closed 10 June 2025; recurs each academic year/semester but the 2026 deadline could not be confirmed on the funder's own page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Adenauer Fellowship for Media and Communication
grants.summary: Supports young journalists from Bangladesh, India, Pakistan and the Philippines (with related country-specific tracks also open to journalists in Indonesia and Malaysia) to pursue a Master's degree in journalism, combining a semester grant, tuition support and study-related travel costs.

amount.note: Semester grant of EUR 500 plus tuition fees up to EUR 6,000, plus study-related travel costs.

grants.notes: Applicants must be 35 or under at the start of postgraduate study, have at least 2 years' relevant work experience, and be fluent in English at C1 level or above. Details were assembled from multiple secondary scholarship-database listings that may conflate slightly different regional tracks; a related 2026 call for Indonesia/Malaysia journalists had a stated deadline of 31 March 2026, already passed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Brings two journalists a year from countries with restricted press and information freedoms to Berlin for a six-month stay focused on rest, protection and recovery, for example after reporting from conflict zones or under state-security pressure. Run annually since 2015, and since 2026 organised independently by the taz Panter Stiftung in cooperation with Reporters Without Borders.

amount.note: Travel costs reimbursed, Berlin accommodation organised, pocket money provided, and free local public transport for up to 3 months; no stipend figure stated.

grants.notes: Six-month Berlin stay (reported as May–October 2026 for this cohort) for two journalists worldwide from countries with restricted press/information freedoms; no language or minimum-experience requirement stated. grants.summary: Sends around ten journalists working in Germany on a group study trip to Washington D.C., Philadelphia and New York to examine the US media landscape, followed by a period of independent research. amount.note: Covers travel, accommodation and programme costs for the 12-day group trip, and partially covers costs for the following 9-day period of independent research.

grants.notes: Open to journalists working in Germany with sufficient English; age and nationality are not restricted. 2026 trip runs September/October 2026; the informal-application deadline (8 March 2026) has passed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Funds two 18-month traineeships per year in the taz newsroom for aspiring journalists with diverse backgrounds who lack classical journalism training or credentials, explicitly welcoming applicants who face discrimination based on origin, religion, gender, gender identity or disability.

amount.note: Each traineeship reportedly costs the foundation approximately EUR 25,000 (donation-funded); this funds the placement rather than being a grant paid directly to the applicant.

grants.notes: 18-month in-house traineeship at taz rotating through newsroom departments; no formal degree or certificate required. 2026 intake (deadline 18 Feb 2026, start June 2026) has already begun; recurs annually. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Czech Republic
grants.programme: Transition Promotion Programme (TRANS) — Local Transition Projects
grants.summary: TRANS is the Czech MFA's framework for supporting human rights, democracy and civil-society development abroad. Local Transition Projects (LTPs) are run individually by Czech embassies and can fund work on rule of law, civic participation, and freedom of expression and information — including freedom of the media — implemented by non-governmental organisations.
grants.eligibleActivity: TRANS's own stated thematic pillars include 'promoting the freedom of expression and information, including the freedom of the media', alongside civil-society support, political participation and rule-of-law themes with no media component — so a newsroom or media NGO could apply for an LTP under that specific pillar, but the programme is not media-exclusive.

amount.note: A CZK 500,000 per-project ceiling for the most recently reported cycle comes from secondary/embassy sources, not from the MFA's own page as captured.

The MFA's own page (captured today, only 268 words) just points to 'an overview of current grant calls' rather than listing terms itself. Reported cycle details (CZK 500,000 ceiling, 8 Dec 2025 deadline for a Mar-Oct 2026 project window, NGO-only implementer, four thematic pillars including media freedom) come from secondary aggregators and individual embassy call pages, not the MFA page captured today; that round's deadline has already passed and no newer cycle is visible on the captured page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A Dutch government fund supporting civil-society human rights work worldwide, disbursed mainly through periodic country-specific calls run by individual Dutch embassies. Priority themes include preventing attacks on and obstacles to journalists and media workers, and the long-term sustainability of independent media outlets, alongside other human-rights themes (e.g. LGBTIQ+ equality, freedom of religion).
grants.eligibleActivity: This is a broad human-rights fund, not media-exclusive, but journalist safety and independent-media sustainability are named as stated priority themes within it, so a media organisation could apply under those specific themes via the relevant embassy's call.

amount.note: Amount varies by embassy/country call; no figure found.

grants.notes: Funding is administered per-country through individual Dutch embassies/consulates, each running its own call with its own deadline (e.g. a Hungary-specific 2026 call had a 1 March 2026 deadline, already passed); there is no single global deadline or application portal. Interested applicants should check their nearest Dutch embassy's page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Rapid-response emergency funding of up to €10,000 for human rights defenders, journalists, activists and organisations facing an active digital threat or attack, covering costs that directly reduce the risk or impact of that attack over a period of up to four months. Digital Defenders Partnership aims to respond to eligible requests within two weeks.

amount.note: Up to €10,000; covers activities for a maximum of four months.

grants.notes: Journalists are explicitly named as eligible applicants alongside human rights defenders, activists and organisations facing digital threats/attacks. Apply via an eligibility check on the funder's site or by emailing team@digitaldefenders.org. grants.funder: Google News Initiative (via JournalismAI / Polis, LSE)
grants.summary: A GNI-supported programme funding news publishers to build and integrate AI-powered prototypes into newsroom workflows over an approximately nine-month programme, with mentoring alongside the funding. amount.note: Reported grant sizes for the 2025-2026 cohort; not directly confirmed on the funder's own page today.

grants.notes: This is a competitive but genuinely fund-for-future-work programme (selected publishers get grants + mentoring to build prototypes), not a prize for past work, so it was recorded despite the 'challenge' name. The most recent round's application deadline (3 Dec 2025) has passed and the next round's dates were not found. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: An annual programme for established U.S. news organisations with a proven business model and a credible plan to expand into a new market, providing roughly $100,000 in grant funding alongside a year of business coaching (delivered via Blue Engine Collaborative) to support the expansion.

amount.note: Reported as roughly $100,000 per selected publisher, plus a year of coaching; not directly confirmed on the funder's own page today.

grants.notes: US-only (not global) despite the source's declared global scope - eligibility is restricted to U.S.-based news organisations. The 2026 round's deadline (7 May 2026) has passed; the programme runs annually, so a new round is expected but dates were not found. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program (Fulbright / J. William Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board, U.S. Department of State)
grants.summary: A non-degree fellowship bringing accomplished, mid-career professionals from designated countries to a US host university for 10 months of graduate-level coursework, professional development and mentoring, with Communications/Journalism (including investigative and broadcast journalism, digital media and public relations) as one of the designated fields. amount.note: No dollar figure confirmed today; program is reported to cover tuition and university fees, a monthly maintenance allowance, a book/supplies allowance, a computer subsidy, round-trip international travel to the host institution (and to English-language training if required), domestic travel to a Washington, D.C. seminar, and supplementary funds for professional activities such as field trips/conferences. Funding does not extend to dependents/family members.

grants.notes: Duration: 10 months, hosted at a US university (specific placement varies by fellow). Deadlines are set per-country by the local U.S. Embassy - for the 2027-2028 cohort these fell between roughly late June and late August 2026, all already passed as of today. The next cycle (2028-2029) is reported to open for applications around May 2027, per third-party embassy/press pages, not the funder's own site. Eligibility generally requires several years of professional experience and English proficiency (exact thresholds not directly confirmed today). Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A nine-month residential fellowship in Cambridge, Massachusetts for 10 science journalists worldwide to deepen expertise in a science, health, technology or environmental specialty while auditing MIT and Harvard courses. Open to full-time staff or freelance journalists with at least three years of science/health/tech/environment reporting experience.

amount.note: Stipend of $85,000 disbursed over 9.5 months, plus additional support for travel, housing and basic health insurance for fellows and their families.

grants.notes: The 2026-2027 cycle opened 15 Nov 2025 and closed 9 Jan 2026 (already passed); those fellows are currently in residence. grants.summary: Supports nonfiction investigative reporting projects by journalists who make their living primarily as freelancers, intended for projects that demonstrate impact, breadth and significance.

grants.summary: A residential fellowship in Stuttgart for artists, researchers and cultural professionals from any discipline who are past the earliest career stage but not yet established, offering a monthly stipend plus project funding.

grants.programme: One-year fellowship for politically persecuted individuals

A journalist facing political persecution can be proposed via the foundation's partner network for a year of safe housing in Hamburg while continuing their journalistic work.

grants.summary: The Council of Europe's European Youth Foundation funds international youth-led NGOs and networks working on human rights, democracy and youth participation, through One-off Youth Co-operation grants (up to €25,000), Long-term Co-operation projects (up to €60,000) and rolling Pilot Activity Grants. Eligible activities explicitly include campaigns, advocacy projects, and the production of educational and other resources and research, alongside international meetings. Applicants must be youth-led (working with people aged 15-30) and based in a Council of Europe member state.
grants.eligibleActivity: EYF's international co-operation grants fund youth-led projects combining international meetings with 'campaigns, advocacy projects, production of educational and other resources, research.' A youth-led human-rights documentation project, media-literacy publication or reporting campaign produced with young people fits directly under this eligible-activity list, provided it is framed as non-formal education/youth participation rather than a straight commissioned news product.

amount.note: Up to €25,000 for One-off Youth Co-operation activities; up to €60,000 for International Long-term Youth Co-operation projects; Pilot Activity Grants available for smaller/rapid-response projects (amount not specified). Pilot Activity applications accepted year-round, at least 3 months before the activity starts.

grants.notes: No snapshot available (funder page returned HTTP 403). Applicant must be a youth-led NGO, informal youth collective or international youth network based in a Council of Europe member state working with people aged 15-30 — a standalone freelance journalist or conventional newsroom without a youth-led structure would not qualify on its own. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Front Line Defenders' Protection Grants provide rapid, practical financial support of up to EUR 7,500 to human rights defenders at risk, covering physical, digital and communications security, legal fees for judicial harassment, medical costs from attacks, and family assistance for imprisoned defenders. Applications are accepted in nine languages and reviewed on a rolling basis with no fixed deadline.
grants.eligibleActivity: Front Line Defenders' own materials state that 'journalists act as human rights defenders when reporting on or investigating human rights issues,' so an at-risk freelance journalist or documenter facing threats, judicial harassment, or attack because of their reporting can apply for a Protection Grant to cover digital/physical security upgrades, legal defence fees, medical costs, or family support — safety and legal costs tied to journalistic human-rights work, not general project funding.

amount.note: Protection Grants are generally not awarded for 100% of the proposed budget.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot confirms the EUR 7,500 cap and what the grant covers (security, legal, medical, family assistance) but does not itself state whether journalists qualify as human rights defenders; that came from Front Line Defenders' own 'Human Rights Defenders' and Journalism pages via search, describing journalists as HRDs when reporting on/investigating human rights issues. This is emergency/protection funding only, not project or core support, awarded rolling with no fixed deadline. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: ILGA-Europe's Documentation and Advocacy Fund gives small grants to LGBTI organisations to document incidents of discrimination, hate crime and other human-rights violations based on sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, producing evidence-based reports used to support advocacy. Running since 2006 as a recurring series of calls, it has historically funded projects in the roughly EUR 2,000-10,000 range.
grants.eligibleActivity: The Fund exists specifically to produce 'evidence-based reports' documenting hate crime, discrimination and other rights violations against LGBTI people — a reporting/documentation activity a journalist could carry out on behalf of, or embedded within, a qualifying LGBTI organisation, since the resulting reports are explicitly meant to feed advocacy on the same violations they document.

amount.note: Historical range across past calls (2006-2016); current call's exact figures not confirmed.

grants.notes: No snapshot available (funder page returned HTTP 404 today); details are from WebSearch of ILGA-Europe's own programme page and secondary sources. Historically the fund runs as periodic calls (14 calls in its first 10 years) rather than a single fixed annual deadline; no confirmed open 2026 call date was found. Applicants must be officially registered LGBTI organisations, or, where none exist in-country, informal/entrepreneurial LGBTI groups — a freelance journalist would need to apply through such a group. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Astraea's International Fund gives flexible general-support grants of USD 5,000-30,000 per year to LGBTQI-led groups with annual budgets under USD 500,000, across Africa, Asia/the Pacific, Eastern Europe/the former Soviet space, Latin America/the Caribbean and the Middle East (the US and Canada are excluded). Grants back a group's own agenda, and Astraea names media-making and narrative control among what it wants LGBTQI groups equipped to do.
grants.eligibleActivity: Astraea states its commitment is to 'equip [LGBTQI activists] with the tools to make their own media and control their own narratives,' so a media, storytelling or documentation project can be funded as general/core organisational work — but only for a grantee that is itself LGBTQI-led (Astraea does not fund groups without LGBTQI leadership), not a general newsroom or unaffiliated freelancer applying on journalistic grounds alone.

amount.note: General support grants per year; applicant organisations' annual budgets must be USD 500,000 or less.

grants.notes: Astraea's grants page returned only a 145-word cookie-consent shell again today (JS-rendered), so this entry relies on WebSearch of secondary grant databases describing the International Fund. General support runs USD 5,000-30,000/year to LGBTQI-led groups (org budget under USD 500,000) in Africa, Asia/the Pacific, Eastern Europe/CIS, Latin America/the Caribbean and the Middle East; the US and Canada are excluded. No specific 2026 deadline was found - treat as a rolling, LOI-based fund. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Fellowship Programme for the ECF Historical Archives
grants.summary: ECF's fellowship funds professional creatives with a research-based practice - including documentary, journalism and audio-storytelling practices - to research its Historical Archives (held at the Historical Archives of the European Union, Florence) and produce a publicly presented or published output within two years. It offers an Academic Research Fellowship (EUR 5,000) and an Artistic Research Fellowship (EUR 10,000, covering travel, accommodation and living costs).
grants.eligibleActivity: The fellowship's eligibility criteria explicitly name 'documentary, journalism or literary practices' among the qualifying research-based practices, so a freelance journalist with a research-based practice and a dissemination plan can use the grant to research ECF's historical archives and turn the findings into a published or presented journalistic/documentary output - archive-based research and dissemination tied to this specific call, not general newsroom reporting.

amount.note: EUR 5,000 for the Academic Research Fellowship track; EUR 10,000 for the Artistic Research Fellowship track (covers travel, accommodation and living costs).

grants.notes: No snapshot available (funder page returned HTTP 404 today); details are from WebSearch of ECF's own culturalfoundation.eu listing via secondary sources. Deadline is 30 September 2026, 17:00 CET; fellowship outcomes must be completed and publicly presented or published within two years of signing the grant agreement. Nationality/residence eligibility was not confirmed, so geoScope is left as global rather than guessed. Two other ECF programmes were checked and not recorded: 'Culture Helps Solidarity' is restricted to people affected by war/displacement (mainly Ukrainian cultural professionals) with no documentation/reporting activity named, and the 'Display Europe' journalism micro-grants call (which did explicitly fund small media outlets/journalists) appears to have closed in March 2024 with no confirmed current cycle. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Western Balkans Program — Democratic Practice / Independent Media Support
grants.summary: RBF provides long-term general-support grants to civil society and independent media organisations in Serbia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Bosnia and Herzegovina working on democratic practice, reconciliation and a European future for the region. Its Western Balkans grantee roster includes cross-border investigative journalism networks such as OCCRP and BIRN. The Fund maintains long-term partnerships and states it has minimal resources for unsolicited applicants, and it does not fund scholarships, fellowships, or grants to individuals.
grants.eligibleActivity: RBF's Western Balkans program names strengthening independent media and investigative journalism as central to its 'democratic practice' priority, and its public grantee list includes the investigative networks OCCRP and BIRN. Because the program is built around long-term partnerships and its own page says it has 'minimal resources available for unsolicited grant applicants,' a newsroom based in Serbia, Montenegro, Kosovo or Bosnia and Herzegovina could realistically approach this as a long-shot general-support relationship rather than a scheduled call.

amount.note: RBF's Western Balkans program budget is reported at roughly USD 4.15 million per year across about 15 grantee organisations (from secondary reporting, not the funder's own page); no individual grant-size figure is stated.

grants.notes: RBF's own Western Balkans page (fetched today) confirms the program's democratic-practice/civil-society focus, its coverage of Serbia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Bosnia and Herzegovina, and that it 'does not fund scholarship or fellowship programs' and offers 'minimal resources ... for unsolicited grant applicants' — but today's own-page text does not itself mention media or journalism. The finding that independent media/investigative journalism (e.g. OCCRP, BIRN) is an actively funded category comes from secondary reporting (Journalism Funders Forum) and RBF's own public grants-search grantee pages, not from today's Western Balkans program-page snapshot. First-ever research pass for this source. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Trag Foundation (with Kosovar Civil Society Foundation, KCSF)
grants.summary: A joint rapid-response mechanism of Trag Foundation and KCSF that provides fast, flexible support to civil society actors, groups and activists across the Western Balkans facing security, legal, digital or psychosocial threats or pressure tied to their public-interest work. Activated February 2026, it is designed to keep organisations and individuals operating when pressure becomes unmanageable on their own.
grants.eligibleActivity: The Fund's own description covers civil society actors facing risk 'due to their work' and support for continuing 'the safety of activists, or the continuity of their activities' and 'their ability to act in the public interest' — language broad enough to cover independent journalists and media workers under legal, digital, physical or psychosocial threat because of public-interest reporting, alongside other civil society actors. It is not addressed to journalists specifically, so the fit depends on presenting the reporting work as public-interest civic activity under threat.

amount.note: No fixed grant ceiling stated on the funder's own page; described as rapid, flexible and targeted support.

grants.notes: Core facts (purpose, activation date of 4 February 2026, joint Trag/KCSF initiative, rolling nature) are quoted directly from Trag's own page fetched today. Secondary corroboration (KCSF's own site) lists the Fund's regional coverage as Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Croatia — broader than Trag's own declared scope (RS + Western Balkans), and eligibility extends to 'both registered and unregistered initiatives and activists.' First-ever research pass for this source.

grants.programme: Public Awareness on Climate Change (Communication Grants)

It offers two tracks: simplified small grants up to EUR 10,000, and two-stage large grants of EUR 20,000-200,000, open to organisations registered in Europe.
grants.eligibleActivity: MFMC's own stated purpose is funding 'communication projects' that advance the transition to a low-carbon economy by influencing public opinion, changing attitudes and spreading information about climate change — not funding emissions-reduction or research projects directly — so a newsroom's climate-awareness journalism, documentary or public-information campaign sits under the fund's primary eligible-activity category rather than an inferred side use. The foundation explicitly excludes projects that target only individual behaviour change, commercial ventures, or research disconnected from a broader communications strategy, and restricts eligibility to organisations registered in Europe.

amount.note: Small grants: simplified one-stage process, up to EUR 10,000. Large grants: two-stage (pitch, then full application), EUR 20,000-200,000. Figures from secondary aggregator reporting (fundsforNGOs), not independently reconfirmed on the foundation's own page today.
